question: What is the SI unit of pressure?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pascal**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
• The **SI unit of pressure** is the **Pascal (Pa)**, named after the French mathematician and physicist Blaise Pascal. 
• **Pressure** is defined as the **force exerted per unit area**. Mathematically, it is expressed as: 
 *Pressure (P) = Force (F) / Area (A).* 
• One Pascal is equivalent to **one Newton per square meter (N/m²)**. This means that if a force of one Newton is applied uniformly over an area of one square meter, the resulting pressure is one Pascal.
